title: 1 · Introduction to DBMS (Unit 1)
learn:
What is a DBMS?

A database management system is a collection of interrelated data (the database) plus programs to access it. Its goal: an environment that is convenient and efficient for storing and retrieving information, while keeping data safe despite crashes or unauthorised access.

Why not plain files?

File-processing systems (one program per task, data in OS files) suffer from: redundancy and inconsistency (same student data in the library and exams files, one copy updated, the other not), accessing anomalies (a new question needs a new program), data isolation (data scattered in different formats), integrity problems (rules buried in program code), atomicity problems (a transfer fails halfway), concurrent access anomalies and security problems.

What a DBMS gives you

Controlled redundancy, consistency, data sharing and integration, integrity constraints, security, atomicity, a query language, concurrency control and data independence. The costs: hardware and software, data conversion, staff training, technical staff and a single point of failure.

Three levels of abstraction

Physical: how data is actually stored. Logical (conceptual): what data is stored and the relationships. View: the part each user sees. Physical data independence means you can change storage without changing the logical schema; logical data independence means you can change the logical schema without rewriting applications.

Architecture

The query processor (DDL interpreter, DML compiler, query evaluation engine) turns queries into low-level instructions. The storage manager (authorisation, transaction manager, file manager, buffer manager) handles disk. Users: naive users, application programmers, sophisticated users and the DBA.

Data models

ER model (entities, relationships; cardinalities one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many), relational model (tables), object-based, record-based and physical models.

quiz.q: Which is a disadvantage of a file-processing system?
Which level of abstraction describes what each user sees?
quiz.why: The view level hides the rest.

quiz.q: Changing the storage structure without changing the logical schema is?
Which component turns queries into low-level instructions?
quiz.why: DDL interpreter, DML compiler, evaluation engine.

quiz.q: A customer has many accounts and each account belongs to one customer. This is?
Who is responsible for overall control of the database system?

lab.task: List four problems of file-processing systems and say which DBMS feature fixes each.
lab.solution: Redundancy/inconsistency → controlled redundancy and a single copy; accessing anomalies → query language (SQL); integrity problems → integrity constraints; atomicity problems → transaction management; concurrent access anomalies → concurrency control; security → authorisation.
